The fluoride framework gives a higher Li:F ratio than LiMgAlF6, which may reduce the O2-releasing La/Zr reaction seen with the best fluoride so far.

proposal.hypothesis: Li3PO4 is a wide-gap (>4 eV) Li-ion insulator with good oxidative stability near 4 V, and it is a well-known interlayer between LLZO and cathodes. Its Li-rich, phosphate chemistry should give a low interfacial penalty against both LiCoO2 and LLZO, and it does not introduce electronic leakage.

LiF is a very wide-gap, electrochemically stable Li-ion insulator with extremely negative formation energy, so it should be chemically inert toward LiCoO2 at 4 V and toward LLZO's La/Zr oxide framework. Its fluoride chemistry gives little driving force for reaction, which should reduce the interfacial penalty relative to the phosphate coating.
proposal.motivation: Li3PO4 (mp-aaaaauhx) gave penalty 0.099 eV/atom (bin 4, not acceptable), with LLZO reacting to form LaPO4, ZrO2 and O2. A different family with a lower reactivity profile is needed to get under the 0.05 eV threshold.

proposal.hypothesis: Li2ZrO3 is a wide-gap Li-ion insulator whose Zr4+ oxide framework is chemically close to LLZO's Zr-O sublattice, so it should offer little driving force to displace La or Zr. Its Li-rich oxide chemistry should also be stable against LiCoO2 near 4 V. Both earlier coatings (Li3PO4 and LiF) drove the same LLZO reaction to La/Zr oxides and O2, so a Zr-O coating should reduce that penalty.
proposal.motivation: Li3PO4 (penalty 0.120, bin 5) and LiF (penalty 0.099, bin 4) both showed the LLZO contact reaction releasing O2 and forming La/Zr oxide products. A coating that shares LLZO's Zr-O chemistry should lower that reaction energy.

proposal.hypothesis: Li3AlF6 is a wide-gap fluoride built on Al3+, which is far harder to reduce than La or Zr and is less prone to releasing O2. The LLZO contact penalty seen with LiF and Li2ZrO3 comes from the coating anion displacing La/Zr and liberating O2. A more stable fluoride framework with a high-valent, non-redox-active cation may lower that driving force toward the 0.05 eV target.
proposal.motivation: LiF (penalty 0.099, bin 4) was the best of the three tested. Its fluoride chemistry gave a lower penalty than the phosphate and Zr-oxide coatings, so a related Al-containing fluoride is the closest step toward improvement.

proposal.hypothesis: Li3BO3 is a wide-gap Li-ion insulator built on B3+, which is very hard to reduce and forms strong B-O bonds. The earlier coatings (Li3PO4, LiF, Li2ZrO3, Li3AlF6) all drove the same LLZO reaction, releasing O2 and forming La/Zr products with penalties of about 0.10 eV/atom. A borate framework with a small, non-redox-active cation and no metal that can displace La or Zr may reduce that driving force. It is also Li-rich, which should keep it stable against LiCoO2 at 4 V.

proposal.hypothesis: Li2O is a wide-gap (about 5 eV) Li-ion insulator built only from Li and O, with no reducible or displaceable La, Zr, or Co cation.
